title: Average of masked randomizations
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, and fix an outcome $x$. For each uniform $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $M(r)=\{i:r_i=0\}$. The average over $r$ of the conditional expectation of $R_rf$ given the coordinates in $M(r)$, evaluated at $x$, equals the product noise operator at rate $1/2$ applied to $f$ at $x$: $\mathbb E_r[E_{M(r)}(R_rf)(x)]=T_{1/2}f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. For uniform $r\in\{0,1\}^n$, $R_rf=\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S$, and $M(r)=\{i:r_i=0\}$, one has $\mathbb E_r[E_{M(r)}(R_rf)(x)]=T_{1/2}f(x)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$; $R_rh=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)h_S$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
